newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-YEBOAH GETS GO-AHEAD TO LEAVE LEEDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YEBOAH GETS GO-AHEAD TO LEAVE LEEDS.

text.p: Disgruntled striker Tony Yeboah has been given the go-ahead to leave Leeds United if he can find another club to pay a transfer fee of around one million pounds ($1.7 million).

The veteran Ghana international, who does not get on with Leeds manager George Graham, has not returned to the English premier league club for pre-season training but is still very keen to continue his career.
"The impression has been given that Leeds would let him go for one million," one source close to the player said on Thursday.
"Tony is 31 but he believes he is still one of the top 10 strikers in the world and wants to prove it."
Yeboah, who joined Leeds from German club Eintracht Frankfurt during the 1994-5 season, had threatened to quit football and return to his native Ghana if he failed to solve his problems with Graham.
He went through a turbulent time last season. At one point he was fined two weeks' pay after ripping off his shirt and throwing it at Graham after being substituted during a league match.
The striker, whose contract is due to run until the end of July 1998, is not prepared to spend another season at the northern club if he cannot get first-team football.

Several clubs have shown interest in Yeboah who is said to be in good physical shape despite his problems. There have been inquiries from clubs in Turkey, Spain and the United States as well from Bundesliga teams.

The Bundesliga might be a good option for the veteran. Yeboah, who is presently in Germany, enjoyed a successful time in the Bundesliga before he left Eintracht under a cloud after an argument with the trainer.
He was the league's joint top scorer in 1993 and 1994.
"He is still very very ambitious," the source said. "In terms of fitness I don't think I have ever seen him looking so good. And he is very positive at the moment."
It is no surprise that Leeds are prepared to let Yeboah go since Graham seems to be taking action on players whose future at the club is uncertain.
This week he dropped five first-team players, including Swede Tomas Brolin, from a tour of Sweden because he had doubts about their future.
Graham decided to leave behind Welsh striker Ian Rush, Carlton Palmer, Tony Dorigo and Brian Deane as well as Brolin from the squad of 20 that departed on Tuesday.
Rush is likely to move on next season, Dorigo and Deane are out of contract and Palmer is unsettled.
